claims.claim_text: The two William L Newman index rows are linked to one high-confidence person entity while both printed rows remain preserved.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The adjacent rows repeat the same exact name, protected identifier, box, and archival location; one row supplies the First Lieutenant rank.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for linking the two source rows, not for assigning an external biography.
claims.temporal_assessment: The source-row linkage establishes no employer chronology.
claims.match_notes: Both immutable rows remain visible; the protected identifier is masked in public data.

claims.claim_text: Earl J Nichelson may be the same person as Earl J Nicholson, but the records remain unmerged pending direct evidence.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The same protected identifier appears with a one-letter surname difference, Second and First Lieutenant ranks, different boxes, and adjacent index pages.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Ambiguous. The shared identifier strongly suggests duplication, but conflicting printed names and file locations require personnel-file review.
claims.temporal_assessment: A plausible promotion sequence does not establish employment or prove that the two file entries are one person.
claims.match_notes: Both person entities and both immutable source rows remain visible; no silent merge is performed.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Lester J Newquist is a probable match to the University of Chicago alumnus and Brown Brothers Harriman banker.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The distinctive exact name appears with a 1936 University of Chicago class year and a contemporary banking chronology beginning at Brown Brothers Harriman in 1936.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable. Name, middle initial, education year, and employment chronology align, but the accessible sources do not explicitly name OSS service.
claims.temporal_assessment: The 1936 employment predates OSS; the exact wartime departure date remains unlocated.
claims.match_notes: The personnel file should confirm the identity and wartime transition before default analytics include the employer.

claims.claim_text: A probable identity match places Lester J Newquist at Brown Brothers Harriman & Co. from 1936.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Lester J. Newquist, who joined the firm in 1936
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A contemporary American Bankers Association personnel notice says Newquist joined Brown Brothers Harriman in 1936 and later became a manager and partner.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable rather than high confidence because the employment source does not explicitly name OSS service.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar employment; not established as the immediate pre-OSS affiliation or last civilian employer.
claims.match_notes: Excluded from default verified-employer analytics until the personnel file confirms identity and wartime sequence.
